paragraph.text: It is a separate map animal type, explicitly retained on Legacy. Ordinary COW features cannot all be transferred automatically.
paragraph.heading: false

paragraph.text: Q16. Does moving an igloo calf immediately wean it?
paragraph.heading: true

paragraph.text: Not necessarily. Moving around two months and beginning the three-month weaning transition are different events.
paragraph.heading: false

paragraph.text: Q17. Will lambs display EUROP condition?
paragraph.heading: true

paragraph.text: Code exists, but SHEEP S5 is disabled by default. Do not assume that full system is released.
paragraph.heading: false

paragraph.text: Q18. Is the new pig nutrition model complete?
paragraph.heading: true

paragraph.text: Parameters and tests exist, but PIG new curves remain disabled. It is not a stable complete replacement for every pig class.
paragraph.heading: false

paragraph.text: Q19. Why is a 600 kg animal not exactly 270 kg meat?
paragraph.heading: true

paragraph.text: 270 kg is a standard reference. Breed, frame, condition and meat genetics adjust individual output.
paragraph.heading: false

paragraph.text: Q20. Why does one slaughter delivery show fractional head units?
paragraph.heading: true

paragraph.text: Orders can use standard-animal equivalents. Check the order rules and final meat kilograms, rather than assuming every unit is a literal head.
paragraph.heading: false

paragraph.text: Q21. Is slaughter guaranteed to earn 12% more?
paragraph.heading: true

paragraph.text: No. That is an annual calibration reference. Current meat prices, season, condition, fees and live quotes determine the result.
paragraph.heading: false

paragraph.text: Q22. Why is an exceptional sire worth far more than its meat?
paragraph.heading: true

paragraph.text: Live valuation includes inherited contributions to offspring. Slaughter still pays for physical product and processing economics.
paragraph.heading: false

paragraph.text: Q23. Why are very old bulls missing from dealer stock?
paragraph.heading: true

paragraph.text: Ordinary stock follows trading purposes and age bands, not equal probability across every age. Existing saves and unmapped species can differ.
paragraph.heading: false

paragraph.text: Q24. Why does a move fail?
paragraph.heading: true

paragraph.text: Check breed, age, sex, castration, capacity, construction, map admission rules and multiplayer permission.
paragraph.heading: false

paragraph.text: Q25. Why are over-age calves not moved automatically?
paragraph.heading: true

paragraph.text: The system warns; the player or automation must arrange movement.
paragraph.heading: false

paragraph.text: Q26. Why are exact weight or health missing?
paragraph.heading: true

paragraph.text: Owned animals often require monitors. Observable condition/Finish can remain visible without them; dealer previews expose additional information.
paragraph.heading: false

paragraph.text: Q27. How can I select finishing cattle in bulk?
paragraph.heading: true

paragraph.text: Use Saved Filters on Manage/Sell. Do not assume a Ready field exists; filter age/sex first and manually review the finishing assessment if necessary.
paragraph.heading: false

paragraph.text: Q28. Why is the Herdsman doing nothing?
paragraph.heading: true

paragraph.text: Check enabled tasks, at least one selected pen, matching filters, destination admission, dealer conditions, funds and permissions.
paragraph.heading: false

paragraph.text: Q29. Why did a price change invalidate an old profit guide?
paragraph.heading: true

paragraph.text: Live and meat prices are linked; feed-price changes alter opportunity costs. Compare the same map, difficulty and price setup.
paragraph.heading: false

paragraph.text: Q30. Why is there no accident compensation?
paragraph.heading: true

paragraph.text: Current F2M removed the old automatic 33% sale-value return. Voluntary disease culling is a different settlement that may recover part of value.
paragraph.heading: false

paragraph.text: Terms and common confusions
paragraph.heading: true

paragraph.text: Live weight: current actual mass, not adult target. Target weight: adult frame target, not Finish reference. Finish weight: commercial reference, not adult weight. Finish / Finish score: reserves/finishing condition, not meat genetics or health. BCS: body condition, not a health percentage. Body reserve: internal stored reserves, not directly saleable meat kg. Ration cover: demand coverage, not storage fill. Milk output %: realized milk potential, not genetics 0-99 or tank liters. Fertility (BCS): conception multiplier, not fertility genetics.
paragraph.heading: false

paragraph.text: DM: dry matter, not wet mass or liters. ME: metabolizable energy, not eaten-liter proportion. CP: crude protein, not a complete protein-quality analysis. NDF / peNDF: fiber/effective fiber, not storage volume. Slaughter reference: finishing reference, not a factory order unit. Dressing rate: live-to-carcass ratio, not saleable fraction. Saleable rate: carcass-to-product ratio, not a price multiplier. Market pass-through: product-market transmission into live prices, not slaughter profit.
paragraph.heading: false

paragraph.text: Cull: active disposal, different from normal commercial sale or accidental death. Heifer: a female that has not calved, not a multiparous cow. Sire: breeding male/father, not any commercial finishing male. Store / Feeder: an animal for further rearing/finishing, not necessarily finished. Weaning: ending milk dependence, not merely moving pens. Legacy: traditional feeding, not automatic access to every new nutrition system. Real-equivalent: a game nutrition mode, not original real-world purchased tonnage. Herdsman: rule-driven automation, not unconditional automatic sale.
paragraph.heading: false
